key_insight: A hybrid physics-assisted neural closure can improve velocity-gradient dynamics modeling in compressible turbulence by learning the unclosed thermodynamic gradient effects, including vibrational non-equilibrium.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate surrogate for compressible CFD closures, especially for high-Mach-number flows where existing models struggle.
method: Builds on phenomenological closures for pressure-Hessian-driven dynamics.
Trains a neural network closure for the inviscid baroclinic tensor generation using a novel tensor basis that can represent non-symmetric features.
Adds a data-driven closure for vibrational non-equilibrium and combines all components into the H-EHEE model.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against DNS across multiple turbulent Mach numbers and showed close agreement with statistics, with the largest gains in highly compressible regimes.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality and coverage of DNS training data, and generalization to untested thermodynamic states or flow regimes may be limited.
paper_title: A physics-assisted deep neural network-based closure framework for velocity gradient dynamics in compressible flows with vibrational non-equilibrium
